clue.text: Branch out, using hard drive provided with playback

annotationWithheld.why: Branch out, using hard drive provided with playback (6): RAM (hard drive) + IF (provided) gives RAMIF, but no clue word gives the final Y, and 'with playback' does not supply it as held
annotationWithheld.clue: Branch out, using hard drive provided with playback

clue.text: Files originated for the auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: something that originated rose, as a rumour rose or arose

explanation.surface: Documents were first created for the accountant checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like the accountant; here it means a hearer, so ROSE is spoken and heard as ROWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Files are lines of things one behind another, the same as rows in a formation.

clue.text: Welsh town supplied with eggs from the country

parts.note: Mold is a market town in north-east Wales
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A town in Wales gets its eggs from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' reads as the countryside, but it defines a nation: the former Soviet republic between Romania and Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is an independent nation in eastern Europe, so a country.

clue.text: Firm support in car …

parts.note: firm, as in held fast or stuck fast
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A company sponsors something inside a car, and the ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 5 down, whose answer is another kind of car.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastback is a car whose roof slopes in a continuous line down to the rear bumper.

clue.text: Fictional captain in South Dakota is sunk

indicators.note: the captain sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for the US state of South Dakota
Captain Cuttle is a retired sea captain in Dickens's Dombey and Son

explanation.surface: A captain from a novel finds himself in South Dakota and is beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the past participle phrase: a ship that has been scuttled is sunk deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle a ship is to sink it on purpose, by opening holes in the hull.

clue.text: … car from the Corn Belt I've overhauled

indicators.note: overhauling a machine means stripping it down and putting it back together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has restored a car bought in America's corn-growing Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhauled' rearranges CORN BELT plus IVE. The Corn Belt is the maize-growing region of the US Midwest; the opening ellipsis continues 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A convertible is a car with a folding or removable roof.

clue.text: Hot water swirling round? Don't mention it!

indicators.note: water swirling round is churned up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone warns against bringing up the subject of hot water going down the plughole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't mention the war!' is Basil Fawlty's famous line in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, so the subject not to be mentioned is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawlty Towers made 'Don't mention the war' a catchphrase, so the forbidden topic is the one meant here.

clue.text: Game on jetty? What could be more eccentric?

parts.note: loo is an old card game
a pier is a jetty jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Playing cards out on a jetty seems a very odd thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a historic card game, not the British word for a toilet here.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy means crazy or odd, so its comparative describes something more eccentric.

clue.text: Detective seen with abrasive old comedian

parts.note: a dick is slang for a private detective
emery is a gritty abrasive, as on an emery board

explanation.surface: A private eye is seen with a rough old joker.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 1970s, known for characters with catchphrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Emery was a British television comic who died in 1983, so an old comedian.

clue.text: Land with a Polish leader

parts.note: Wales is a land, one of the nations of the UK

explanation.surface: A country goes along with someone shining up a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the verb to shine; it is the nationality, pointing to Lech Wałęsa, Solidarity leader and later president of Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lech Wałęsa led the Solidarity movement and became President of Poland, a Polish leader.

clue.text: A French woman, retiring one in company, not fearless

parts.note: un is French for a, the masculine article
her stands for a woman

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the piece runs backwards
the numeral goes inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman, shy and withdrawn among others, is lacking in courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside CO to make CIO; 'retiring' turns that to OIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Unheroic means lacking heroism or courage, so a fair stand-in for not fearless.

clue.text: This, grammarians say, is a no-no

definitions.text: This, grammarians say, is a no-no

parts.words: This, grammarians say, is a no-no
parts.note: a no-no is a forbidden thing, but read literally 'no-no' is two negatives, the construction grammar teachers forbid

explanation.surface: Grammarians declare that something is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works both ways: 'no-no' shows two negatives side by side, and that construction is itself what grammarians call a no-no.
explanation.definitionFit: Using two negatives, as in 'I don't know nothing', is condemned by grammarians.

clue.text: New York theatre, say?

parts.note: the Empire is a common name for a theatre or music hall
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is a theatre in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York theatre' looks like one phrase, but New York is the definition: its nickname is the Empire State.
explanation.definitionFit: The Empire State is the long-standing nickname for New York State.

clue.text: Free cinema popcorn — initially consumed for free

indicators.note: freeing the letters of the word cinema lets them fall into a new order
initially means take the first letter of the word popcorn

parts.note: ate means consumed, as food is eaten

explanation.surface: Free popcorn at the cinema gets eaten at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' opens the clue as the anagram signal (EMANCI from CINEMA) and the definition is the last word, with 'for' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to set free, as slaves were liberated.

clue.text: Scratch teams tied in ballpark?

indicators.note: a scratch team is thrown together, so the letters are assembled in a makeshift order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Makeshift sides draw a game at the baseball stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ballpark' looks like a stadium, but a ballpark figure is a rough one, so 'in ballpark' means roughly reckoned.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimated figure is approximate, a ballpark number rather than an exact count.

clue.text: Alexander Selkirk's tongue

indicators.note: 's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the end of the first name and the start of the surname run together, the possessive saying the name holds the word

explanation.surface: A question of what language the real-life castaway spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'has': the name has the word inside it. Alexander Selkirk, the Scottish castaway behind Robinson Crusoe, would fittingly speak Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for Gaelic, a language, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Sensational turn, OK?

explanation.surface: A tumbler's somersault is checked to see whether it was fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: turning OK round gives KO, the usual abbreviation for a knockout in boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is informally something stunning, so a sensational person or thing.

clue.text: A scholarly work, in my opinion

explanation.surface: Someone says that, as they see it, a book is learned.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large heavy book, often a learned one; 'to me' is a phrase meaning as I see it.

clue.text: Remark made by first person in French resort

indicators.note: the pronoun sits inside the name of the resort

parts.note: Menton is a resort on the French Riviera near the Italian border
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A comment is made by the first visitor at a Riviera resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made by' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention something is to remark on it in passing, and a remark is a mention.

clue.text: Clergyman with prayer designed to catch crook

indicators.note: catching something means enclosing it, so the bend goes inside
something designed is laid out in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
a crook is a bend, as in the crook of the arm

explanation.surface: A churchman prays as part of a plan to capture a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed' gives PREARY, which 'to catch' opens round the bend. 'Crook' tempts as a criminal for the clergyman to catch, but it is the bend, as in the crook of an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebendary is a canon of a cathedral who receives a stipend, so a clergyman.

clue.text: Couple on river in boat, as seen in illustrations

indicators.note: the couple and the river go inside the boat

parts.note: Noah's ark is the most famous boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the couple comes before the river

parts.note: a couple is two
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A pair of people on a river in a boat appear in book pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As seen in' is a link: the illustrations in a book are its artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Artwork is the collective term for the pictures and illustrations in a publication.

clue.text: Female with new hat and close-fitting dress

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: new signals that the word hat is made anew in a different letter order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman with a new hat is wearing a tight dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges HAT to EATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting dress, often straight and unbelted.

clue.text: Side order of synthetic cream

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them, here differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A side dish of artificial cream is requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side order' reads as a restaurant extra, but 'Side' is a football team and 'order of' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester City is an English Premier League football club, and a side is a team.

clue.text: Burden a person usually conceals

indicators.note: the two words conceal the answer inside them, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: People generally keep their troubles to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, as in the onus of proof.

clue.text: Craft that's shipshape going to Inishmore, Inishmaan and Inisheer?

parts.note: trim means neat and in good order, like shipshape
these are the three Aran Islands off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A well-kept boat makes a trip out to the Irish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to' is a link joining the two pieces; the three island names together define the Aran Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a boat with three hulls, so a craft.

clue.text: Cut across to Detroit

indicators.note: the cut grass lies across the word, enclosing it

parts.note: mown means cut, as grass is
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a short cut through to Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: Detroit's nickname Motown, from Motor Town, also named its famous record label.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is the nickname for Detroit, from its car industry.

clue.text: Sound travels quickly in boats

parts.note: a ding is a ringing sound, as of a bell
to hie is an old word for to go quickly, so hies means travels quickly

explanation.surface: Sound carries fast across the water to small boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a homophone signal, but it is simply DING, a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinghies are small open boats, often used as tenders.

clue.text: Race pickets

explanation.surface: Two words placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes is a horse race with prize money from entry fees; pickets are pointed posts driven into the ground.
